title: Fix six open newcomer findings on the firstmate explainer page
summary: Fixes the six open findings on the generated firstmate page for newcomers. It adds distinct decider and worker terms, a t10 ready-to-ready explanation, a reopened tag fix, a rewritten f2 note, an "in scope" glossary entry, and an early next-step link. Content changes go in the study JSON; xtask/src/site.rs changes only for rendering, with tests and a CHANGELOG entry.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check the page's wording and links, using site tests and the site build.
Site tests are added for items 1, 3, 5 and 6; cargo test, clippy and fmt are required.
Every new firstmate statement cites a claim sourced at the pinned SHA.
Criteria check the rendered HTML, not just that the data files exist.
The change stays within the study JSON, site.rs and CHANGELOG.md.
Criteria are checkable by cargo test and `cargo run -p xtask -- site`.
The new wording is written for a reader with no prior context.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience: newcomers to the page at https://doodla.github.io/athena/, and the rater who reads it cold.
Item 1: 'agent' stays the deciding agent and the worker agents get 'worker'. t4's trigger is reworded so the merge-landing event is decided by code or by a named event, not by the agent.
Item 3 is read as relabelling reopened's kind or adding an explanation. Which of the two depends on how site.rs renders kind.
t10 is assumed to be explained, not remodelled, unless the firstmate source at the pinned SHA says otherwise. I could not read that source here.
The set of governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) does not need to change.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`. Site tests pass and show three things. First, no transition marked 'decided by agent' has a trigger that names another decider's event, so t4's trigger is split or re-attributed. Second, the deciding agent and the worker agents use two different terms, and the page says which one 'decided by agent' means. Third, the page contains a glossary entry for 'in scope'.

Run `cargo test`. A site test shows the reopened state no longer carries the bare 'terminal-success' tag, or the tag is explained on the page. A second site test shows a link to the next step appears in the HTML before the first transition card.

The t10 card explains why the yolo merge is drawn ready to ready while t4 takes a merge to done, citing a claim whose source is firstmate at the pinned SHA. If that source shows the drawing is wrong, model.json changes instead, with the citation.
The f2 model-limit note is removed, or rewritten in plain words a newcomer can follow. No newcomer-facing text mentions a model limit without explaining it.

'In scope' is defined where it first appears in intro.json (green terms, the 'what' text and the t10 summary), and a glossary entry for it cites a claim sourced at the pinned SHA. Every new statement about firstmate cites an existing or new claim.
Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site`. It builds the page and validates the study without error. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for this change. The items already fixed in bca96fc (captain, yolo, home, ra1 to ra6, lede study id) are not reworked.

out_of_scope: Restructuring the front page around Athena
Rework of the captain, yolo, home, ra1 to ra6 and lede study id fixes from bca96fc
departures: The work has six items, a claim-sourcing check against the firstmate source, and site tests. That makes it somewhat larger than the typical job, so cost, time and the pass rate are shifted slightly worse than the reference.
